song.title: Goodbye Winter, Hello Spring!
song.author: Mark and Helen Johnson
song.summary: An upbeat and energetic introduction to the new season. Verse by verse it allows us to let go of all things winter, and to give a warm welcome to spring. A really singable, catchy song to get us all in the mood for celebration. ‘Life is waking up!’
song.teachingTips:
• Lots of energetic physical warm-ups will get the children in the right mood for singing this upbeat song. 
  • Encourage the class to count the 4 bars of introduction (1 2 3 4, 2 2 3 4, 3 2 3 4 etc.) so that they are ready to come in in bar 5. It’s good practice to do this even if you are using the Words on Screen program.
  • The melody of the verse should be straightforward to learn as the second phrase is pretty much the same as the first. However, notice the difference between the rhythm for ‘Hello spring’ and ‘lighter days’. Clap these rhythms and practise them a few times separately to ensure they are accurate.

assembly.title: Super Seeds
assembly.description: This assembly encourages us to look at the potential of seeds for new life and growth and also provides an opportunity to explore our own potential.

assembly.title: Light and Colour
assembly.description: This assembly encourages us to open our eyes to the colours of springtime, talking about our favourite colours, noticing the extra daylight and appreciating nature's use of colour and light.

assembly.title: Extra Energy
assembly.description: What wakes you up in the morning? From birdsong to sprouting leaves and Easter eggs, this assembly helps us to celebrate all the energy of springtime.

assembly.title: Metamorphosis
assembly.description: Looking at change and understanding that there are things to be enjoyed at every stage of life.

assembly.title: People Who Care
assembly.description: The ideal assembly to help us to focus on, appreciate and celebrate all those who help and care for us.

assembly.title: The World Around
assembly.description: From the tallest trees, to the something you can only see with a microscope, this assembly encourages us to notice, appreciate and be thankful for the world around us.

assembly.title: It’s Challenging
assembly.description: By looking at changes in nature, this assembly helps us to explore change and how it can sometimes be difficult.

assembly.title: Happy Endings
assembly.description: This assembly explores setbacks we might encounter in our lives and the characteristics needed to overcome them.

assembly.title: Feeling Hopeful
assembly.description: This assembly explores the meaning of hope and what it will take to realize our ambitions for the future.

assembly.title: Feeling Awake
assembly.description: This assembly uses The Parable of the Sower to reflect on what is needed to be ‘awake and ready for action’ in school.

assembly.title: Eggs Galore!
assembly.description: This assembly explores the symbolism of eggs and their place in Pancake Day, Easter and Passover celebrations.

resources.title: Exploring Tonality
resources.content:
[{"key":"f85e48bfb5ded696","layout":"icon-bullet","attributes":{"body":"
  • To hear the difference between major and minor keys (tonality)
  • To improvise a tune in a major or minor key
  • To compose a short melody with lyrics in a major or minor key
","title":"What’s achievable","noMargin":false,"image":"https://assets.sparkyard.com/uploads/icons/green-star-1614702483w2iKm.png"}},{"key":"deb1370ab0078a99","layout":"icon-bullet","attributes":{"body":"

Sets of chime bars (one with C D E F G and another with C D Eb F G); large books/folders

","title":"What you need","noMargin":false,"image":"https://assets.sparkyard.com/uploads/icons/blue-wrench-16147025258WedI.png"}},{"key":"cb2ee07dc151adbe","layout":"wysiwyg","attributes":{"body":"

Explore what makes this such a cheerful song. Children might mention the lyrics. Discuss the contrast between winter's dark and dreary, cold and frosty weather and spring's warm and lighter days, sunshine and blue skies. Write these words up on the board in Winter and Spring columns.

Explain to the class that every piece of music is built on a scale or key, i.e. a set of notes that go up and down. In C major these notes are C D E F G A B C. All play or sing them up and down. But in C minor, two of the notes are changed – the E becomes E♭, and the A becomes A♭. Now play or sing C D E♭ F G A♭ B C. Can the children hear the difference? How would they describe this? Does it change the mood? Major keys are often described as sounding ‘happy’ – whereas minor keys can be thought of as ‘sad’. Can the children hear if this song is in a major or minor key? (It’s in C major.)

Set up two sets of chime bars behind a screen (some large books or folders would do). One with the notes C D E F G (a mini or ‘micro’ scale) and one with the notes C D E♭ F G. Ask for two volunteers to improvise a short tune (starting and finishing on C) on each of the sets of chime bars. Can the rest of the class tell whether they are playing a major or a minor tune?

","title":"","noMargin":false,"background_color":null}},{"key":"28b6b6bbf0321b88","layout":"icon-bullet","attributes":{"body":"

Split the class into small groups, some with minor-key chime bars and some with major-key ones. Using the appropriate words from the board, and any other winter/spring words they want to add, can they write their own Winter or Spring Song?

","title":"Step It Up!","noMargin":false,"image":"https://assets.sparkyard.com/uploads/icons/u1873-1614695091mFFrP.png"}},{"key":"0c59ff9da7d66ce7","layout":"icon-bullet","attributes":{"body":"

Listen to some other songs in major keys, such as The Beatles’ Let It Be or Leonard Cohen’s Hallelujah. Now listen to some in minor keys, such as Pink Floyd’s Another Brick In The Wall or The Beatles’ Eleanor Rigby. Can the children suggest songs that they know and work out if they are in a major or a minor key?

","title":"Listen","noMargin":false,"image":"https://assets.sparkyard.com/uploads/icons/listen-01-1615991956LRT6z.png"}}]
resources.summary: Explore musical ‘mood’ by learning about tonality and playing scales in major and minor keys. Step this up a level by composing simple winter or spring songs.

resources.title: Playing Classical Music (Spring)
resources.content:
[{"key":"8de421d31e95fe11","layout":"wysiwyg","attributes":{"body":"

Make it a routine to play some classical music at the beginning of the day – perhaps when the children are taking off their coats, settling in the classroom or entering an assembly. Here are a few ideas: 

  • Ballet of the Unhatched Chicks (Mussorgsky)
  • The Lark Ascending (Vaughan-Williams)
  • On Hearing the First Cuckoo in Spring (Delius) 
  • Spring from The Four Seasons (Vivaldi) 
","title":"Music","noMargin":false,"background_color":null}}]

resources.title: The Arrival Of Spring
resources.content:
[{"key":"e6936f3f06a10794","layout":"wysiwyg","attributes":{"body":"

David Hockney (b. 1937) recently made a series of works responding to the changing colours of woodland (Wold Woods, Yorkshire) throughout the four seasons. He created oil paintings, charcoal drawings and iPad drawings, and recorded films as part of this series of work. 

How could the children use the influence of Hockney's work to respond to the colours and changing nature of spring? 

  • Take photos of the school grounds (field/flower beds/nature area) thoughout the seasons to see how things have grown and changed. (Record in a school/class calendar to carry on throughout the year.)
  • Record films of the school grounds. 
  • Incorporate technology to embrace Hockney's style: use iPads or tablets to create spring drawings and play back the creation of these to watch how they form the finished work. 
","title":"","noMargin":false,"background_color":null}}]

resources.title: Rainbow Dance
resources.content:
[{"key":"1dcd9b7908e4c9ce","layout":"wysiwyg","attributes":{"body":"

Rainbow Dance <\/strong>by Len Lye (1936) is a combination of experimental film, jazz and dance and is an inspiring watch! After watching the film, encourage the children to think about what movements spring brings: plants growing; raindrops falling; children running, jumping and skipping in the playground. Then, think about the colours of spring. Create a contemporary dance piece that expresses this collision of movement and colours to showcase in one of your spring assemblies. <\/p>\n","title":"","noMargin":false,"background_color":null}},{"key":"279afe7bf7efd6b1","layout":"video","attributes":{"url":"https:\/\/www.youtube.com\/watch?v=AHN9IHGQxk8","title":"Rainbow Dance","active":false,"noMargin":false,"background_color":null}}]

resources.title: Planting Project
resources.content:
[{"key":"b1349c66455145d6","layout":"wysiwyg","attributes":{"body":"

Abraham Cruzvillegas (b. 1968) is a conceptual artist who creates sculptures and installations using found, recycled objects. 

In homage to Cruzvillegas' Empty Lot exhibition at Tate Modern, organize a planting project; ask the children to bring a small plant from their garden or a seed or a bulb from home. Find an area in the school garden, or use a colletion of indoor pot plants for the classroom. Plant the bulbs and seeds and study their growth throughout the season. Think about whether this could be photographed or recorded some way through drawing. How could you make it into a sculptural project? 

","title":"","noMargin":false,"background_color":null}}]

resources.title: Spring celebrations
resources.content:
[{"key":"1b2cc4940756aede","layout":"wysiwyg","attributes":{"body":"

The arrival of spring is an important time of year, with celebrations taking place to mark the occasion all around the world. What spring traditions and celebrations<\/strong> do the children already know about? Find out about how Easter is celebrated in different countries. Other spring festivals include the Songkran Water Festival in Thailand, the Hanami cherry blossom festival in Japan, and the colourful Holi festival in India. Locate these places on a globe or atlas and ask groups to research a particular celebration and present their findings to the class.<\/p>\n","title":"","noMargin":false}}]

resources.title: Accepting Change
resources.content:
[{"key":"02c960800411ac7f","layout":"wysiwyg","attributes":{"body":"

Make a list of all the changes that occur in nature, throughout the seasons. In the springtime in particular, there are so many changes to be thankful for! Explain that all of these changes happen for a reason. 

Now make a list of all the other changes that can happen in life e.g. moving house or school or having a new member of the family. As a class, discuss the fact that these can be both positive and negative experiences. Discuss ways in which we can develop resilience and ‘see the bigger picture’, just as we might be sad to see the trees lose their leaves in the autumn, but we know there will be new life in the spring. 

","title":"","noMargin":false}}]
